newsitem.title: TURKEY: Lower Turkish bond rates lead to deposit rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Lower Turkish bond rates lead to deposit rate cuts.

text.p: Turkey's small and medium banks cut their rates on lira deposits in all maturities by between one and 10 points this week, following a sharp fall in bond yields and lower money market rates in the last two weeks.

Bankers said state banks and big private banks were also expected to reduce their deposit rates in line with the bond yields which stabilised after plunging by as much as 20 points in the last two weeks with support from the central bank's move last Monday to cut its money offer rates.

The downtrend in t-bill and bond yields began in the last days of 1996 after the government decided to raise witholding tax on interest income to 12 percent from from 10 on state securities to be issued this year.
This fuelled demand for outstanding papers with the help of another cabinet decision to delay income tax on interest income from state papers for another year to 1999.
Witholding tax on deposit rates was also raised to 12 percent in 1997 from previous five percent.

Bankers said the deposit rate cuts were a result of the general downtrend in bond yields, adding that the seven-point increase in witholding tax further sharpened the fall in net net returns on deposits.

After the cuts, banks' rates fell to a range between 75-80 percent for one-month deposits, 80-83 percent for three-month deposits, 90-93 percent for six-month deposits and 95-99 percent for one-year deposits, including the witholding tax charge.
Bond yields edged slightly higher across the board to between 91-99 percent this week, but bankers said the move was in limited ranges.
Total deposits in Turkey jumped 109 percent to 2,900 trillion lira on December 20, 1996, when compared with end-1995.
Total bond portfolios of banks stood at 806 trillion lira on December 20, 1996, up 212 percent from end-1995.
